analysis.title: Market Perspectives: 10 Minutes That Bears Watching, Changing Seasons, Changing Outlooks
key_insights: Q2 2026 earnings grew about 30% on core (51% unadjusted) year over year, yet some of the fastest growers got muted price reactions. The team reads this as a shift in market leadership.

AI remains transformational, but the team argues the AI value chain should no longer be treated as one trade. Many AI data centre buildout stocks remain below their highs despite strong earnings growth and positive revisions.
Bipartisan state-level moves to slow data centre buildouts (Texas, Pennsylvania, Virginia, California) add political constraints on top of grid reliability, permitting and local capacity limits.

If construction slows while suppliers add capacity, pricing power in memory, optical components and power equipment is likely to erode. The long-term buildout stays intact, but the near-term earnings revisions cycle becomes less exceptional.

Hyperscalers could benefit disproportionately from slower data centre construction. They already have builds in progress, so near-term free cash flow pressure is lower, and approval costs could fall as supply bottlenecks ease.
The team sees the early stages of a late cycle. Earnings growth stays positive but the rate of change slows, and the expected return for taking incremental risk is lower than earlier in the cycle.

August ISM Manufacturing was 54.6, just below the 55 threshold. Historically, readings of 55-60 were followed by a mean 12-month S&P 500 return of 7.2% (median 7.8%), and readings above 60 by a mean of 1.9% (median 2.6%).

Market-implied policy rates are rising across all large developed economies for the first time in four years. The team reads this as the start of a global rate-hiking cycle, and notes that tighter policy has historically preceded market volatility.
Rising rates, stubborn inflation and a commodity bid are corroborating late-cycle signals. Leadership is Energy, Materials and Healthcare, with software also finding a bid.

The S&P 500's three-year annualized return is 21.6%, in the 94th percentile of data going back to the 1960s. Further gains need elevated earnings growth, falling inflation, easing geopolitical risk and a neutral central bank.

Bearish sentiment exceeds bullish at a 0.68 reading, about 1.5 bears per bull. The team says such extremes have often preceded favourable near-term forward returns, so it is not positioning defensively.
The team is not calling for a bear market. Positive returns are the base case, but expectations should be moderated from the high-double-digit returns of recent years.

Positioning: the portfolios stay invested with a cyclical tilt but are more balanced. They have cut some AI capex beneficiaries, re-engaged hyperscalers, and hold interest-rate-sensitive Financials, quality software, measured Energy and lower-beta AI exposure. They remain underweight Consumer Staples.
The team would turn more defensive if evidence shows growth rolling over.

sector_views.rationale: Measured exposure that provides optionality when uncertainty rises. Energy is a leading sector quarter to date on geopolitical strife.
Portfolios hold interest-rate-sensitive Financials as policy rates rise.
AI exposure is lower but still healthy. Some AI capex beneficiaries were trimmed, hyperscalers are being increased, and high-quality software is held.
Growth has not degraded enough to justify a more defensive stance.
Cited as a best-performing sector quarter to date and part of the defensive leadership. No explicit portfolio weight is given.

earnings_insights: Q2 2026 S&P 500 earnings grew about 51% year over year unadjusted and about 30% on core, as reported by the team using Bloomberg data. The team says acceleration from these levels is unlikely.

Some of the fastest-growing companies in Q2 2026 saw indifferent price reactions. Many AI data centre value chain stocks remain below their highs despite significant earnings growth and positive revisions.
The team expects the near-term earnings revisions cycle for AI suppliers to be less exceptional if data centre construction slows and supplier capacity grows.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above-average growth, yet the best-performing sectors are Energy and Healthcare rather than broad cyclicals.
Just below the 55 threshold and short of 60, which is associated with the end of the cycle. Positive 12-month equity returns remain reasonable, but with lower amplitude.

macro_indicators.reading: near levels last touched in May 2007
macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields are elevated while growth is strong, consistent with tightening conditions.

macro_indicators.reading: rising across all large developed economies
macro_indicators.interpretation: The first unanimous upward direction in four years, which the team reads as the start of a global rate-hiking cycle.
Elevated caution is already embedded, which has historically favoured near-term forward returns.

risk_factors: State-level political and permitting constraints on data centre buildouts broaden and alter orders, pricing and earnings revisions across the AI supply chain.
Strong results stop producing positive price reactions in former leadership groups.
Expected rate increases turn into sustained tightening, which historically precedes volatility.
Economic growth rolls over, which would confirm the late-cycle progression.
Elevated trailing three-year returns (94th percentile) leave less room for further gains.

tension_points.bull_case: AI remains transformational and the long-term buildout stays intact. Some beneficiaries still show strong free-cash-flow growth and positive earnings revisions.
tension_points.bear_case: State-level political resistance and permitting limits slow buildouts while suppliers add capacity. Pricing power in memory, optical components and power equipment erodes, and the near-term revisions cycle becomes less exceptional.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Strong results again producing positive price reactions in former leadership groups, or the data centre restrictions failing to broaden and alter orders, pricing and revisions.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive returns are the base case. Bearish sentiment at 0.68 is elevated, which has historically preceded favourable near-term returns, and growth is still strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Policy rates are rising globally, the S&P 500's three-year return is at the 94th percentile, and the expected return for added risk is lower in a late cycle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that economic growth is rolling over, which would raise conviction that the late cycle is progressing and warrant a more defensive mix.
